pageCache.pageTitle: Abbotswood Junior School - Ethos and Values
pageCache.text:
Ethos and Values
Our School Values
Abbotswood is a happy and caring school community built on five core values: Stickability, Teamwork, Aspiration, Respect and Stretch. To encourage children to remember our values, they spell out the word STARS which is integral to our school logo:
Stickability – We succeed because we never give up.
Teamwork – We achieve more by working together.
Aspiration – We work hard to achieve our goals and dreams.
Respect – We value and care for each other and our environment.
Stretch – We have the courage to challenge ourselves to achieve our best.
At Abbotswood, we aim to provide a happy, secure and rich learning environment where children strive for the highest standards in all that they do. We endeavour to create conscientious, independent learners who are able to persevere when faced with new challenges and children who are respectful of others. We promote our Abbotswood Values throughout the curriculum so that children recognise ‘It Really Does Matter’.
Our behaviour reward system promotes our five core values. Children who have successfully and consistently demonstrated each of the values become one of our Abbotswood All-Stars.
Ethos
At Abbotswood, we believe every child is unique, valued and full of potential. We are committed to creating a safe, inclusive and inspiring environment where children are encouraged to be curious, confident and kind.
Our ethos is built on our school values. We nurture a strong sense of community where every voice is heard and every achievement is celebrated. Through high-quality teaching, enriching opportunities and strong relationships with families, we support each child’s academic, emotional and social development.
Together, we strive to foster a love of learning that lasts a lifetime, preparing our children to thrive not only in school but in the wider world.
Our School
Ethos and Values

Maths
At Abbotswood, our Maths curriculum is designed to inspire our children to think mathematically. Carefully sequenced lessons support children to build and develop their conceptual understanding of Maths, ensuring children develop fluency in the fundamentals of mathematics which enables them to reason and problem solve successfully. Regular opportunities for children to revisit core knowledge supports them to confidently apply their skills to a range of problem solving contexts. Children who grasp mathematical concepts quickly are given rich problems to extend their knowledge and understanding, encouraging them to ‘dive deeper’ into mathematical concepts with more sophisticated reasoning. Our AFL driven approach to teaching and learning recognises that every child has different needs and must be challenged or supported at the earliest opportunity to help them become confident and fluent mathematicians.
Subject Curriculum Overviews

​Music
At Abbotswood, our Music curriculum has been designed to instil the ‘Power of Music’ set out in The Model Music Curriculum . It states that, ‘Music is creative, collaborative, celebratory and challenging. In our schools, music can bring communities together through the shared endeavour of whole-school singing, ensemble playing, experimenting with the creative process and, through the love of listening to friends and fellow pupils, performing.’
At Abbotswood, our aim is that every child benefits from an outstanding Music education which is fun, creative, inspiring and innovative. Lessons are tailored to each child’s individual needs and musical interests to enable them to achieve their full potential. Through our Music curriculum, children will develop a critical engagement with music, allowing them to develop progressive performance, composing and listening skills. We are committed to making Music a creative strength and presence throughout the school so that children experience ‘the joy of music making’.
Click to view the Music Medium Term Progression Overview
Click to view the Music Progression Sequence
Subject Curriculum Overviews

Art
At Abbotswood, Art is taught through our integrated, topic based curriculum, ensuring it is woven into a rich learning journey that provides a purpose, context and audience for learning. We aim to teach Art in fun, creative ways that ensure the children are stimulated through creativity and imagination. Our Art curriculum is designed to provide a progressive education in the visual arts, emphasising the development of technical skills, creativity, and critical thinking. Through focused instruction in drawing, sculpture, and painting, we aim to build a strong foundation in the essential elements and principles of Art, while encouraging students to explore and express their individual ideas.
Our Art curriculum is designed to teach a clear progression of skills, from basic concepts to more challenging techniques, ensuring that every child has the opportunity to build on their prior knowledge and experience. Our aim is to foster both technical progress and creative exploration, allowing children to confidently express their ideas and grow as artists. In addition to skill development, we encourage children to engage with the cultural and historical contexts of Art, fostering an appreciation for diverse artistic traditions and artists. Through carefully planned and structured lessons, we strive to create a supportive environment where every child can succeed and develop a lifelong appreciation for the visual arts.
Click to view the Art Medium Term Progression Overview
Click to view the Art Progression Sequence
Subject Curriculum Overviews
Art

Computing
We are passionately dedicated to developing independent, lifelong learners at Abbotswood Junior School. With this at the heart of our school values, we are committed to giving children a unique Computing learning experience which will allow them to excel and thrive in an ever-changing digital world. At Abbotswood, our constantly evolving Computing curriculum is designed to challenge, motivate and inspire our children to become confident, creative and analytical ‘Digital Enthusiasts’.
Our three curriculum strands of Computer Science, Digital Literacy and Information Technology are interwoven throughout all aspects of our rich, carefully sequenced curriculum, equipping our children with the skills and knowledge they require to proceed confidently, competently and responsibly on life’s journey within a digital world. Alongside this, we follow the Education for a Connected World framework, linked to our PSHE curriculum, ensuring children will thrive in the digital environment by developing effective strategies for staying safe and making a positive contribution online.
Click to view the Computing Medium Term Progression Overview
Subject Curriculum Overviews
Computing

DT
At Abbotswood, DT is taught through our integrated, topic based curriculum, ensuring it is woven into a rich learning journey that provides a relevant context and ‘end-user’ to make learning purposeful. Our Design and Technology curriculum is crafted to be rigorous, exciting, and relevant, aiming to inspire and equip children with the skills necessary to become innovative problem solvers. Through engaging and challenging projects, we aim to develop children’s ability to think critically by evaluating and understanding the principles of design and the processes involved in creating effective and innovative solutions.
We aim to cultivate children’s ability to approach problems systematically, think creatively, and develop practical solutions while considering the needs of the intended user. Through collaborative and individual hands-on activities and projects, students will learn to identify problems, generate ideas, prototype, test, and refine their designs. By providing a comprehensive and inspiring Design and Technology education, we aim to empower our children to become confident, creative, and capable individuals who are ready to tackle the challenges of the future.
Click to view the DT Medium Term Progression Overview
Click to view the DT Progression Sequence
Subject Curriculum Overviews

English
“The limits of my language are the limits of my world” (Ludwig Wittgenstein).
Our English curriculum has been designed to empower all children to achieve their potential as readers and authors. We want children to enjoy and appreciate literature for all of its rich variety whilst absorbing the artistic styles and golden threads that run through the many areas of fiction and non-fiction. They will hone their craft as authors, learning to control the reader, taking them on journeys, entertaining them and leaving them speechless.
Through a range of approaches, we will expand children’s vocabularies and language to give them the voice they need to articulate their ideas, challenge perspectives and feel a sense of belonging in the world.
Our English curriculum weaves reading, grammar and writing together, through a rich integrated learning journey that provides a purpose, context and audience for learning. The English Learning Journey is planned around exploring the ‘golden threads’ of a ‘rich read’ text (the key composition and effect themes and conventions), allowing children to develop a depth of understanding of each genre and become masters of their craft. In addition, we have daily reading lessons, with an oracy focus, that allow children to improve reading fluency while also developing their inference skills, exploring language and learning together. After all, learning is a social activity: “[It is] through others that we become ourselves” (Vygotsky).
At Abbotswood, our English Curriculum will remove the limits that a lack of language can create and give them access to the world in all of its splendour.
Subject Curriculum Overviews

Geography
Through our Geography curriculum at Abbotswood, we aim to inspire a lifelong curiosity and fascination in the world and its people. Our integrated, topic-based approach ensures that Geography is woven into a rich learning journey that provides children with a context, purpose and real audience. Each unit is driven by a ‘Big Geographical Question’ that encourages pupils to think critically, explore diverse global perspectives and develop the mindset of a ‘geographer’.
Children are encouraged to ask questions, weigh evidence and think creatively about the world around them. Fieldwork is an essential part of our curriculum, giving children the opportunity to explore their local area and compare it with other regions of the world. This hands-on learning experience helps children develop valuable skills and a deeper understanding of Geography in a real-world context. We aim to build resourceful, active citizens who are equipped with the confidence and skills to make informed decisions and contribute positively to their communities and the world around them. By fostering critical thinking and a global perspective, we prepare our pupils to engage thoughtfully with the world and its challenges.
Click to view the Geography Medium Term Progression Overview
Click to view the Geography Progression Sequence
Subject Curriculum Overviews
Geography

History
At Abbotswood Junior School, our History curriculum is designed to ignite curiosity, foster critical thinking and inspire a deep understanding of the human past. We believe that history is not only the study of events but also the exploration of ideas, cultures and the diverse experiences that have shaped our world. Through a rich and inclusive curriculum, children at Abbotswood will gain insight into both global and local histories, developing an appreciation for key historical figures and their impact on the present and future.
History is taught through our integrated, topic based curriculum, ensuring it is woven into a rich learning journey that provides a purpose, context and audience for learning. Each unit is driven by a ‘Key Historical Question’ with the aim to empower children to become informed, empathetic and engaged historians who are able to question, analyse and challenge historical narratives with confidence. This mindset will prepare them to be active participants in a rapidly changing world, while nurturing a lifelong love for learning and exploration.
Click to view the History Medium Term Progression Overview
Click to view the History Progression Sequence
Subject Curriculum Overviews

MFL
A high-quality language education should foster children’s curiosity and deepen their understanding of the world. At Abbotswood, we follow the Language Angels programme of study to ensure we offer a relevant, broad, vibrant and ambitious French language curriculum that will inspire and excite our pupils. We aim for all children to be able to:
develop a genuine interest and positive curiosity about foreign languages, finding them enjoyable and stimulating.
speak with increasing confidence and fluency, finding ways of communicating what they want to say, including through discussion and asking questions, continually improving the accuracy of their pronunciation and intonation.
begin to write using the variety of grammatical structures that they have learnt.
feel willing and able to continue studying languages beyond key stage 2, becoming life-long language learners.
Click to view the French Medium Term Progression Overview
Click to view the French Progression Sequence
Subject Curriculum Overviews

PE
At Abbotswood Junior School, we recognise that physical education and sport are essential parts of a child’s life and key to their future development and well-being. We want all children to find enjoyment in physical education through a wide range of sporting opportunities provided to them. We aim to present all children with opportunities to work in partnerships and teams, compete against themselves and others whilst building self-confidence and perseverance.
Our broad and balanced physical education curriculum is designed to ensure all children develop fundamental movement skills and become increasingly competent and confident in a range of sports. Progressive and logically sequenced learning objectives aim to provide stimulating, enjoyable and appropriately challenging learning experiences for all pupils.
We prepare and support pupils towards healthy and active lifestyle choices for their future mental and physical well-being.
Silver = OSA (Outdoor Sports Activities)
Invasion sports- Handball, Netball, Basketball, Rugby, Football, Invasion Skills (LKS2)
Creative- Dance and Gymnastics.
Net/Wall- Tennis and Net/Wall Skills (LKS2)
Strike/Field- Cricket, Rounders, Strike Field Skills (LKS2)
Athletic- Indoor and Outdoor Athletics
Click to view the PE Medium Term Progression Overview
Subject Curriculum Overviews

PSHE
PSHE education helps children and young people to stay safe, healthy and prepared for life's opportunities. At Abbotswood, we follow the curriculum sequencing and objectives set out by The PSHE Association, alongside The Medway RSE resources, which supports our teaching of Relations and Sex Education. Our aim for a high quality PSHE curriculum, set out by The PSHE Association, is that we teach children to foster lifelong aspirations, goals and values. PSHE is about giving every child an equal opportunity to develop the skills and knowledge they need to thrive now and in the future. This includes helping them to deal with critical issues they face every day, such as friendships, emotional wellbeing and change, giving them a solid foundation for whatever challenging opportunities lie ahead.
Click to view the PSHE Medium Term Progression Overview
Subject Curriculum Overviews

RE
Religious Education contributes to children’s spiritual, moral, social, cultural and intellectual development. At Abbotswood, our RE curriculum follows the Hampshire Agreed RE Syllabus ‘Living Difference IV’ which seeks to introduce children to what a religious way of looking at, and existing in, the world may offer in leading one’s life, individually and collectively. Our core aim is to encourage children to respect the religious commitment of others and embrace that people have the right to hold different religious beliefs, helping them to celebrate and embrace difference through open, fair minded inquiry.
Our RE curriculum is designed to provide a rich and wide range of learning experiences, giving children opportunities to develop concepts and skills that will help them to make sense of their own experiences and beliefs, and to see that there are common values and concerns across all religions and non-religious worldviews, even though the expressions of these may be emphasised in different ways.

pageCache.text:
Internet Safety - Advice for Parents
E-Safety and keeping safe online
The internet is a wonderful place and is a valuable part of our children's lives, but we also know it is vital to teach our children about how to use the internet safely and how to stay safe online so they can fully enjoy what it has to offer. At Abbotswood, we ensure that our curriculum teaches our children about the importance of being safe online, how to identify risks online and how to keep themselves safe. We do this through our computing and PSHE curriculum, which are based on the framework Education for a Connected World (insert link https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/education-for-a-connected-world), through our computing lessons, in assemblies and through whole-school events such as Safer Internet Day and Anti-Bullying Day. You can read about our Online Safety Policy here (insert policy).
All our pupils at Abbotswood also sign a Pupil Technology Charter. This explains how we expect them to use technology while at school and the safety rules we expect them to follow. The Pupil Technology Charter can be found here (insert pupil charter).
Staying SMART
We teach our children to be SMART when they are online.
(insert image of SMART from ChildNet net: https://www.childnet.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/SMART-rules-Poster-A3.pdf )
Safe – to keep their and other people’s personal information safe and not share it online.
Meet – to be careful with people they only know online and tell a trusted adult if someone online asks to meet up, asks for personal information, asks for photos or asks for photos.
Accept – to think carefully before clicking on links, adverts or pop-us, and to not accept friend requests from people they don’t know.
Reliable – to know that not everything online can be trusted and understand that there are such things as misinformation, disinformation and fake news. It is important to check facts in different places and talk to someone about what they have read or seen.
Tell - to tell a trusted adult if anything online makes them feel worried, upset or confused.
We use a monitoring and filtering system called Senso for our school devices that means we can see what our pupils are accessing on the internet and how they are using it. This means we can make sure any websites they use and web searches they make are safe and appropriate for them.
E-safety Ambassadors
Pupils who are interested in computing and helping others stay safe online are elected as E-safety Ambassadors. These E-Safety Ambassadors work with our ICT Manager, Mr Pentland, to share key messages with their classes about online safety, take the lead in Safer Internet Days and are part of our pupil Online Safety Group. They also remind children about telling someone if they see anything on the internet that worries or upsets them.
Have a look at some of the safety posters we created for Safer Internet Day 2025 all about protecting ourselves from online scams and phishing.
How can you help?
To help you keep your children safe online, the NSPCC suggests that you work as a TEAM. These are four easy steps to follow that can help keep your children safe when they are online.
Talk about staying safe online
Explore their online world together
Agree rules about what is okay and what is not
Manage your family's settings and controls
It is important to make these conversations about being safe online regular and a part of daily life. Talking to them openly and regularly will encourage your children to talk to you if they ever feel worried or unsure about anything linked to being online.
How can you start the conversation?
It can feel hard to start a conversation about being safe online with children and there will be some conversations that will be more difficult than others. But it's so important to have them, so you can support your child with their worries or issues.
You might find it useful to start with a family discussion about being online and what you expect from your children. This can help to set boundaries and agree what's appropriate.
Sometimes you might need a more specific conversation about something you’re worried about, a particular online safety topic, or an app or website that your child wants to use.
If you're not sure where to start, there are some great guides about beginning these conversations.
The NSPCC guide to talking to your child about online safety here. (INSERT with link https://www.nspcc.org.uk/keeping-children-safe/online-safety/talking-child-online-safety/) This guide has advice about conversations with different age groups and suggestions about how to talk about some specific topics such as cyberbullying.
The UK Safer Internet Centre has a collection of guides here (INSERT link https://saferinternet.org.uk/guide-and-resource/parents-and-carers) to help you talk to your children about different electronic devices including phones, tablets and games consoles.
How might you know something is wrong?
Having regular conversations with your children will help you feel confident about what they are seeing, doing and reading online.
There are some signs that might show that something online has upset them or made them worried. Some signs to watch out for are:
They become very secretive especially about what they are doing online
They are spending a lot of time on the internet and social media
They switch screens on their device when you are close by
They are angry or withdrawn after using the internet or sending messages
They have lots of new phone numbers or email addresses on their devices
If you spot any of these signs, try to have a conversation with your children. It is also important to give them other options. This could be by speaking to a trusted adult family member, a trusted teacher or a pastoral member of Room 5, or by speaking to Childline on 0800 1111 or on the Childline website (INSERT LINK https://www.childline.org.uk/). Children who are worried about their activity on apps or online games can contact Childline 24 hours a day, online and over the phone.
If you are concerned or have any questions about how to start discussing safe online use with your children, you can contact the NSPCC Helpline on 0808 800 5000 or visit the NSPCC website (https://www.nspcc.org.uk/ ).
What technology should you allow?
There are no exact rules about the right age to give your children access to technology. Every child is different and every child matures in their own time. Parents know their children best. It is up to them to decide what access they give and when to give children more independence online.
The NSPCC recommends thinking carefully about:
The age you give your children their own device.
The access your child has to online platforms and services.
The NSPCC has advice here (https://www.nspcc.org.uk/keeping-children-safe/online-safety/access-to-technology-for-different-ages/) for parents when thinking about introducing children to technology and advice for different age groups.
Social Media and the law
If your child has a Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat or other online accounts, then they should be at least 13 years old. You can find information about the Online Safety Act and the safety requirements social media companies have to follow to help keep children safe here (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/online-safety-act-explainer/online-safety-act-explainer)
How can you set parental controls?
Parental controls can help you feel that your children are as protected as possible when online. It is useful to talk to your children first about which sites, apps or games they are using online and then decide the controls you want to put in place.
The NSPCC website has information and guides here (https://www.nspcc.org.uk/keeping-children-safe/online-safety/parental-controls/) to help you set up controls including for WiFi, computers and search engines.
The UK Safer Internet Centre has some useful guides here (https://saferinternet.org.uk/guide-and-resource/social-media-guides) that can help you understand how these social media sites work. They also provide information about safety features, how to set and use parental controls and how to report anything concerning.
Internet Matters are also practical guides available here (https://www.internetmatters.org/parental-controls/?filter-search=roblox) to help set parental controls for social media and gaming sites including Fortnite, Roblox and YouTube.
How can you help your children stay safe with their first phone?
Children get their first mobile phone at different ages. However, usually more children start to get phones as they get closer to secondary school age because they are getting prepared for more independent travel to and from school. This can feel like a worrying time for parents and carers. The NSPCC has worked with Vodafone to create a toolkit to help parents and carers when their children are getting their first phone. It provides advice and top tips. You can find it here (https://www.vodafone.co.uk/help-and-information/nspcc-phone-safety-toolkit)
At Abbotswood, pupils may bring mobile phones into school to use outside of school time; for example, to contact parents/ carers when they are walking to and from school without an adult. They are not permitted to use mobile phones during school time which includes lesson time, break and lunch and at before and after school clubs. We expect pupils to turn off their mobile phones and to keep them in their lockers. Abbotswood takes no responsibility for any mobile phones brought into school by pupils. If a pupil is found to have used their mobile phone during school time, their phone will be confiscated by a member of staff and the pupil’s parent/ carer will be informed. The mobile phone will be kept at the office and the pupil’s parent/ carer will need to collect this at the end of the day.
Where can you get help and advice from?
Here are some useful websites that can help you get advice and support .
NSPCC – insert webpage link
UK Internet Centre – insert webpage link
Report Harmful Content – this allows you to report harmful content. Insert webpage link.
SWGfL - Insert webpage link.
Internet Safety - Advice for Parents
